items.title: Google Publishes 2026 Responsible AI Report + AI Impact Summit
items.summary: Google released its 2026 Responsible AI Progress Report detailing multi-layered governance across the full AI lifecycle. Key highlights: SynthID verification in Gemini App has been used over 20 million times to identify AI-generated images, video, and audio. Circle to Search and Lens now detect scam messages, helping millions avoid fraud. The report covers how Google operationalizes its AI Principles from initial research through post-launch monitoring. Announced alongside the AI Impact Summit 2026 in India.
items.relevance: SynthID hitting 20M uses shows AI content verification is becoming mainstream. The scam detection in Circle to Search is practical AI safety that affects daily life. Google's governance framework is worth skimming if you're thinking about responsible AI practices for AVA — especially around health data and kid safety.

items.title: Global Memory Chip Shortage — HBM Sold Out Through 2026, Prices Soaring
items.summary: AI demand has triggered a full-blown memory chip crisis. Micron stock surged 44% as the company announced a $200B manufacturing expansion. All HBM4 and HBM3e inventory is sold out through December 2026, with shortages expected into 2027. HBM demand will increase 70% year-over-year in 2026, consuming 23% of total DRAM wafer output (up from 19%). The shortage is inflating prices on everything from laptops and smartphones to automobiles — not just AI hardware.
items.relevance: The downstream effects matter: laptop and phone prices going up means hardware refresh cycles get more expensive. For AI API pricing, this could slow the cost compression trend — if compute hardware gets more expensive, API prices might plateau or increase. Worth factoring into any budget planning for AVA's AI backend costs.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.32 — Opus 4.6, Agent Teams, and the File Name Controversy
items.summary: Claude Code v2.1.32 shipped with Opus 4.6 support and a research preview of 'agent teams' for multi-agent collaboration. Meanwhile, the v2.1.20 change that hid file names from progress output continues to generate backlash. Boris Cherny repurposed verbose mode as a compromise — showing file paths for reads/searches without full thinking output. Developers argue this breaks verbose mode's original purpose. The core tension: Anthropic optimizes for longer agentic runs while power users need granular visibility.
items.relevance: Agent teams is the headline feature — multi-agent collaboration in Claude Code means you could have specialized agents working on different parts of AVA simultaneously. The file name controversy is a practical heads-up: if you update, verbose mode behaves differently now. Check your settings.

items.title: ADA 2026 Diabetes Care Standards — Updated Tech and Pediatric Guidance
items.summary: The American Diabetes Association published its 2026 Standards of Care with updated guidance on diabetes technology, obesity medications, nutrition, preventive care, hospital management, pregnancy, pediatrics, and older adults. Separately, ADA announced 2026 Pathway to Stop Diabetes grant recipients, including research using computational models to identify CGM patterns as early warning signals for progression from healthy glucose levels to prediabetes.
items.relevance: Updated pediatric guidance is directly relevant for Kaislyn's care. The CGM-as-early-warning research could eventually expand CGM use beyond diagnosed diabetes into prevention — a massive market expansion that would bring more investment and innovation to the CGM space. Worth checking the specific pediatric tech recommendations.

items.title: CGM Market to Hit $49.3B by 2036 — 10.6% CAGR
items.summary: New market forecast projects the global glucose monitoring device market will grow from its current base to USD 49.3 billion by 2036, reflecting a 10.6% compound annual growth rate. Growth driven by rising diabetes prevalence, aging populations, and rapid technology advances. The expanding use of CGMs by non-diabetic wellness consumers and the shift toward automated insulin delivery systems are key accelerators.
items.relevance: A $49B market means the CGM ecosystem will keep getting better, cheaper, and more competitive. For AVA Type 1, this validates building on CGM data — the installed base of CGM users is only going to grow. The wellness consumer crossover also means more app developers entering the space, which means both more competition and more potential integration partners.

items.title: Alibaba Qwen3.5 — 200 Languages, 5x Faster Agents, 60% Cheaper
items.summary: Alibaba launched Qwen3.5 handling text, images, and video across 200 languages. AI agent deployment is 5x faster than predecessors and 60% cheaper than Qwen3. Part of China's Lunar New Year AI blitz alongside ByteDance's Doubao 2.0 (reasoning matching ChatGPT/Gemini) and Zhipu's GLM-5 (744B open-source model trained entirely on Huawei Ascend chips with zero US semiconductor dependency). All three companies pushing hard on autonomous web-navigating agents.
items.relevance: GLM-5 on zero US chips is a geopolitical milestone — sanctions aren't stopping Chinese AI development. Qwen3.5's 60% cost drop continues the trend of AI getting radically cheaper. If you need a budget model for batch processing or less critical tasks, these Chinese models are increasingly viable alternatives.

items.title: Former GitHub CEO Launches 'Entire' — $60M to Rebuild Dev Workflows for AI Agents
items.summary: Thomas Dohmke launched Entire with the largest-ever seed round for dev tools ($60M, backed by Felicis, Madrona, Microsoft M12). The thesis: Git tracks what changed but not why. AI agents generate reasoning and decision paths that disappear when sessions end. Entire's first open-source product is a Git-aware CLI that automatically captures AI agent context during development. Dohmke argues current dev workflows were designed for human-to-human collaboration and can't be retrofitted for human-to-agent work.
items.relevance: This solves a real pain point — when Claude Code makes changes, the 'why' behind decisions doesn't survive in Git history. The open-source CLI could be worth trying in your AVA workflow. At $60M seed, investors clearly think developer tooling for the agent era is a huge gap. Watch for the first release.
